claim: Download buttons use exact asset URLs only when the latest GitHub release matches the website source commit.
sandbox: intercept matching GitHub release metadata and require the detected button to equal the fixture asset URL; reject a stale source commit

claim: A release manifest requires macOS arm64, macOS Intel, Windows x64, and Linux x64 assets with SHA-256 checksums tied to one source commit.
sandbox: generate a manifest from six fixture packages; assert four platform entries and that every package URL and checksum identifies the candidate commit; reject a stale commit

claim: The one-line installer rejects a bad SHA-256 checksum before installing and installs a matching artifact.
sandbox: run the production shell installer with local manifest/download shims; assert mismatch leaves no binary and a valid hash installs exact bytes

claim: Conflicts take priority, and folder-only evidence never establishes convergence.
where: landing evidence explanation, desktop board, README
sandbox: summarize deterministic folder readings containing a conflict and a reading without provider pending evidence

claim: Folder scans inspect metadata without reading or changing file contents.
where: landing, desktop privacy dialog, privacy page, README
sandbox: scan a temporary file whose contents look like a conflict marker; assert it is not classified from contents, remains byte-identical, and convergence stays unknown

claim: Folder scans stop at 50,000 entries and depth 16.
sandbox: assert production scan bounds and prove a conflict filename below the depth boundary is not inspected

claim: Syncthing checks accept loopback or .local endpoints and reject remote hosts.
sandbox: validate remote HTTPS, IPv4, IPv6-loopback, and .local endpoints in the production core; submit http://[::1]:8384 through an instrumented desktop form and require one production probe

claim: Android and iPhone visitors are told the observer is desktop-only and are not offered an unusable Linux download.
sandbox: fresh Pixel 5 and iPhone 13 contexts at 390 x 844; assert one desktop-only message, hidden primary download, all three facts inside the viewport, and no GitHub release lookup

claim: Source credentials, paths, and readings stay in unencrypted local app storage with no telemetry request, and removal deletes the saved source.
where: desktop privacy dialog, privacy page, README
sandbox: save and remove a fixture source; assert its credential uses namespaced localStorage, every request is same-origin, and removal clears the saved source

claim: A finding opens the owning local tool for the fix without changing the observer reading.
where: landing how-it-works section, desktop sample, README
sandbox: load the desktop sample, click Open sync tool, require the fixture local URL in a new window, and assert the conflict reading remains

claim: The running desktop app refreshes configured sources every 30 seconds.
sandbox: mock the native probe, add a source after launch, advance the browser clock by 30 seconds, and require a second probe

claim: The website uses no cookies or analytics and contacts only itself plus the disclosed GitHub release API.
sandbox: record a fresh landing visit; assert no cookies and no request origin beyond same-origin and api.github.com

claim: Local Sync Observer is free software under the MIT License.
sandbox: read the shipped LICENSE and assert the MIT permission grant is present

claim: The sample demo is isolated from real observer data.
where: landing demo action, /demo, desktop sample mode
sandbox: fresh browser context; load /demo; assert the sample is visible, only the demo namespace exists, then reset it

claim: The sample demo sends no data to third parties.
sandbox: fresh browser context; record every request while loading and reading the sample; assert every request is same-origin

claim: The sample demo works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: dedicated browser context; visit /demo, wait for its service worker, set offline, reload, and assert the sample conflict remains visible

claim: If GitHub cannot provide release details, the website shows a release-page link.
sandbox: intercept the GitHub release request with a failure; assert the fallback message and release-page link

claim: The production Syncthing check reports configured folders, local and connected-device pending items, offline devices, and conflicts.
where: landing headline and Syncthing coverage, desktop board, README
sandbox: run the production probe against a controlled loopback Syncthing server; assert four configured folders, summed pending items, an offline device, and conflict priority

claim: Each reading shows a last-good value when established, missing provider details, and the checks used.
where: landing how-it-works and status limits, desktop board
sandbox: run the production probe against controlled complete and incomplete provider responses; assert last-good, unreported pending state, Unknown, and coverage text

claim: The observer uses GET-only provider checks and does not rename, delete, or change observed files.
where: landing method and figure, terms, README
sandbox: snapshot controlled folder paths and bytes, run the production Syncthing probe, assert every provider request is GET and every fixture remains present and byte-identical

claim: The desktop tray names the current overall reading without exposing filenames or paths.
sandbox: inject a deterministic native Conflict reading; assert the UI sends only the overall state and attention count to the production tray command

claim: The demo and desktop observer require no product account.
sandbox: open the demo from a fresh browser context; assert a working conflict reading without sign-in controls or cookies

claim: The website removes a cached GitHub release response after one hour.
sandbox: seed an expired release entry, make the GitHub request fail, then assert the fallback appears and the expired localStorage entry is deleted

claim: Nextcloud desktop log checks report conflicts, offline status, pending activity, and completed syncs without changing the log.
where: landing coverage, desktop source setup, privacy page, README
sandbox: read four controlled Nextcloud desktop-log fixtures; assert conflict, offline, pending, and completed states, a last-good value, missing pending counts, and unchanged log bytes

claim: The isolated demo shows a Syncthing conflict-copy example and a Nextcloud desktop-log example with pending activity.
sandbox: fresh browser context; open /demo/?demo=1 and assert the named Syncthing conflict-copy and Nextcloud pending-log explanations plus both visible provider rows and states

claim: The desktop app checks a sync tool only after the user adds a local source and selects Save and inspect.
where: /demo sample note, desktop empty state and source setup
sandbox: fresh desktop-app browser context with an instrumented native bridge; assert zero provider probe commands before and during setup, then assert one Syncthing probe after Save and inspect
